_comment: Hand-authored. Small tables whose readers were found while mapping scenes and corridors.

regions.name: Story screen: palette, then the text-reveal attribute values
regions.description: $8396: LDY #$0D / LDA $8472,Y / STA $0180,Y / DEY / BNE - 13 palette bytes to $0181-$018D for the intro story screen ($86E8, 'LONG AGO AN ALIEN RACE...'). Then $83F7: LDA $847F,Y with Y = 0-2 or 3-5 into $14, and $C036 ($D5F8) fills eight attribute bytes at PPU $23C0 + row with it - 05 0A 0F then 5F AF FF, stepping each band of text from palette 0 up to palette 3. The two tables overlap by one byte ($847F is both the 13th colour and the first attribute value), and together they end exactly on the code at $8485.

regions.name: Song header $00 at $9932: code follows
regions.description: Song table entry 70 points here. $97E4 reads a header's first byte, and when it is $00 it pushes the pointer and RTSes, so execution continues at $9933 - the 'song' is code (registered in dispatch.json extra_seeds). This byte is that marker.

regions.name: Song header $00 at $9939: code follows
regions.description: Song table entry 71 points here. $97E4 reads a header's first byte, and when it is $00 it pushes the pointer and RTSes, so execution continues at $993A - the 'song' is code (registered in dispatch.json extra_seeds). This byte is that marker.

regions.name: Song header $00 at $993E: code follows
regions.description: Song table entry 31 and 68 points here. $97E4 reads a header's first byte, and when it is $00 it pushes the pointer and RTSes, so execution continues at $993F - the 'song' is code (registered in dispatch.json extra_seeds). This byte is that marker.

regions.name: Song header $00 at $9ADF: code follows
regions.description: Song table entry 69 points here. $97E4 reads a header's first byte, and when it is $00 it pushes the pointer and RTSes, so execution continues at $9AE0 - the 'song' is code (registered in dispatch.json extra_seeds). This byte is that marker.

regions.name: Drop cycle: 4 item types
regions.description: LDA $44 / INC $44 / AND #$03 / TAY / $81F2 LDA $8229,Y - four entries, cycled - stored to the new object's $0680. Values $15 $0C $0C $0B; a $0B is swapped for $0C when bit 6 of $04AE (weapon 11's level) is set. Read when $8221,$42 is zero.

regions.name: By terrain class under an object: 16 entries
regions.description: $81D9 LDA $822D,Y with Y = the value bank 6 $8435 (far-called through $8006) returns: the terrain nibble of the cell under the object, read from the packed map at $0400 and AND #$0F, so 0-15 - sixteen entries. Non-zero decrements $43 and returns. Meaning of the entries not established.

regions.name: Table read at $8176, 120 bytes
regions.description: $8176 LDA $823D,Y, zero skipping, with Y from the caller - not bounded by code. The extent is structural: it starts where the 16-entry table at $822D ends and runs to the code at $82B5, and nothing else in bank 1 reads into it. A LEAD.

regions.name: Tile-block ids 13-14: no block
regions.description: Bank 2's tile-block pointers are read by $D7F9 as $8024 + 2 x id; ids 13 and 14 land here and hold $0000, between the 13-entry group ($8024) and the 21-entry group ($8042).

regions.name: Two tables by $51, eight apart
regions.description: $82D0: LDY $51 / LDA $8291,Y -> $0680 and $82D6: LDA $8299,Y -> $0668, in the handler at $82C0. $8291 is the RTS ending the code before, so the reads start at Y = 1. The four tables after ($82A1, $82A9, $82B1, $82B8, also indexed by $51) share one pattern with these: entries 4 and 5 are equal in every one of them when counted from each read base, which says the bases really are the table starts and Y runs 1-7. Which object this is, and so what $51 means when it runs, is NOT established.

regions.name: Table read by $8573
regions.description: LDA $8577,Y ($8573) -> $8812, with Y from JSR $880C when it returns carry set. $8577 plus the Y reaching data starts here; the extent to the code at $858E is structural and Y's range is NOT established.

regions.name: Sound played on picking up items 12-22
regions.description: $872A: TAY / LDA $87AF,Y / BEQ / JSR $C030 (play a sound), with Y the item number, reached only for items 12 and up ($86BE CMP #$0B sends 0-10 to the weapon code and 11, the Enemy Eraser, to $8711). So the bytes read start at $87AF + 12 = $87BB. The branches after it match the manual's item icons: 12 copies max life $47 into $48 (Energy Tank), 13 calls $C033, 14 increments $4A (Gun), 15 increments $4B (Shield). The 11 is structural - it ends where $87C6's reads begin.

regions.name: Weapon level masks and increments
regions.description: $86BC splits weapon w (0-10) into byte Y = w / 4 of $04AC-$04AE and X = w mod 4, then AND/CMP $87C6,X (03 0C 30 C0: that weapon's two level bits - all set means level 3, so the pickup becomes chips instead) and ADC $87CA,X (01 04 10 40: one level). Two 4-byte tables, ending exactly where the next table, $87CE, begins.

regions.name: Chip maximum by level: 12 words
regions.description: $8820: LDA $46 / ASL A / TAY / LDA $87D4,Y / STA $4E / LDA $87D5,Y / STA $4F - the chip maximum the status screen prints after CHIP MAX, chosen by the level in $46 (which a password restores from $04A8). Values 50, 100, 150, 200, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400, 4000, 6000, 30000. The manual's Red Lander 'raises Power Chip maximum' - a step up this table. 12 entries, ending where the door records at $87EC begin - a structural bound.

regions.name: Door cells: 8 x [cell][tile][?][exit mask]
regions.description: $866E-$86AC walks these with X stepping by 4 to CPX #$20 - eight records, which is exactly this stretch. For each: the terrain nibble of cell byte 0 (packed map at $0400) must be $0E, and byte 3 ANDed with $54 - the room's exit bits from map byte 1 ($80 north, $40 west, $20 east, $10 south) - must be non-zero; then bytes 1 and 2 go to $15 and $17 and the cell is redrawn through $8812. The masks run $80 $80 $40 $40 $20 $20 $10 $10: two door cells per side.

regions.name: Tile-block id 0: no block
regions.description: Bank 3's base in $D842/$D84A is $8020, so id 0 lands here: $0000. Ids 1-6 follow at $8022.

regions.name: Tile-block id 15: no block ($FFFF)
regions.description: $8020 + 2 x 15: $FFFF, between the ids 1-6 at $8022 (plus the code at $802E, which ids 7-14 would land on) and ids 16-63 at $8040.

regions.name: OAM template: one sprite
regions.description: $873C: LDX #$04 / LDA $870C,X / STA $0203,X / DEX / BNE ($873E) - these 4 bytes to $0204-$0207, sprite 1: Y $54, tile 0, attributes 0, X $50.

regions.name: OAM template: two sprites
regions.description: $8B0F: LDX #$08 / LDA $8B1A,X / STA $0203,X / DEX / BNE ($8B11) - copies these 8 bytes to $0204-$020B, hardware sprites 1 and 2: Y $30, tile 0, attributes 0, X $30, and Y $B8, same tile and X.

regions.name: Boss object type, by corridor
regions.description: Bank 3 $91B8: LDY $51 / LDA $913A,Y -> $71, then (skipped for corridor 21 by CPY #$15 / BEQ) LDA $9151,Y ($91C3) -> $72, the type bank 3 $92E5 spawns for the boss phase and $92EE waits on. Values by corridor 0-22: 06 40 45 2E 46 23 47 06 49 18 19 2D 41 4C 25 24 2F 06 48 4D 26 4D 4F. Corridor 1's $40 is CONFIRMED against hardware: the owner's savestate of the corridor 1 boss fight (Fleepa) has $51 = 1, $72 = $40 and slot 23 of type $C0, drawn exactly as type $40's handler draws it (41/41 sprites). Types $40 and $41 share that handler, so corridor 12's $41 is presumably Fleepa again - a lead. The other entries are not tied to names. The 23 is a structural extent (to the next table), and the last entries may never be read; a LEAD on the extent.

regions.name: Types $2D-$2F: spawn attributes
regions.description: $93FA (bank 3 JMP entry $8012) is the handler of types $2D, $2E and $2F - bank 6 $907A is only a far call to it: LDY $0500,X / LDA $94E2,Y ($93FF) -> $0560, the object's attribute byte. $94E2-$950E is the handler's own code, and $94E2 + $2D-$2F lands exactly here: three bytes, ending on the table at $9512. CORRECTION to 'which objects run the handler is NOT established' - found while building the pieced-object composites, where it gives these types their palette.

regions.name: Fleepa (types $40/$41): eight small tables for $952E
regions.description: Read by bank 3 $952E (bank 3 JMP entry $8015): LDA $9633,Y and $9635,Y with Y = the object type ($9533, $9539) - $9633-$9672 is the handler's own code, so the data lies at Y = $40-$41; ORA $9677,Y with Y = ($41 AND $10) / 16 (sprite flip 00/40); $9679,Y with Y = $16 (two tiles); $967B, $967E and $9681,Y with Y = $07B8,X (three entries each: attributes, a tile offset added to $87, a tile); and $9684,Y with Y = $17, 0 or 1 ($964B). 2+2+2+2+3+3+3+2 = 19 bytes, exactly the gap, ending on the tile block at $9686. CORRECTION to 'which objects run this handler is not established': types $40 and $41, whose bank 6 handler $9081 is only a far call to bank 3 $8015 -> $952E. Type $40 is Fleepa, corridor 1's boss (owner's savestate). Four of these tables are the pieces $952E draws on top of metasprite 131 through $CC34: $9679 (132/133, drawn twice mirrored), $967B/$967E/$9681 (attributes, base-tile offset and id 123 or 25 by $07B8) and $9684 (134/135, 24 pixels lower). Rebuilt from them, all 41 of Fleepa's sprites in the savestate's OAM match.

regions.name: Item or shop stock, by map sub-id
regions.description: $814E: LDY $5E / LDA $A377,Y / STA $55, with $5E the sub-id a map record of kind $20 or $40 carries (tools/tgl/worldmap.py). The map uses sub-ids 0-67 and this stretch is exactly 68 bytes, bounded by code on both sides. Values 0-$11. $55 is an ITEM: in an item room (kind $20, byte 0 bit 7 clear) the type-$31 object spawned on the layout's metatile 6 takes its icon from $55 (bank 2 $84EE), so this is the item, 0-17 = the 18 icons. In the shop screens it is instead an index: screen 6 reads $A067 + 3 x $55, screen 2 $A04E + 5 x $55 - which is why sub-ids 58-67 hold 0-4. CORRECTION to 'what $55 selects is NOT established'. docs/labyrinth.html#items lists every room.

regions.name: Value by weapon level ($3D = 1-3)
regions.description: $8A8C: LDY $3D / LDA $8A96,Y. Y is the selected weapon's level, 1-3, so the read starts one byte early on the JMP operand before it. Three bytes, ending on the code at $8A9A - the handler whose five level tables start at $8ADE.

regions.name: Five 3-byte tables by weapon level ($3D = 1-3)
regions.description: $8AA4: LDY $3D (the selected weapon's level) then LDA $8ADD,Y -> $05D8, $8AE0,Y -> $06C8 (the base tile), $8AE3,Y -> $C13B, and at $8AD0 $8AE6,Y ANDed with $41 and $8AE9,Y -> $0578 (collision flags). Five bases three apart, and Y is 1-3, so each read starts one byte early - $8ADD is the handler's own RTS and is never read as data (level 0 is an unowned weapon, skipped by $FD77). 5 x 3 = 15 bytes, ending exactly on the code at $8AED. The same overlap trick as the weapon stat tables at $8701.

regions.name: Types $18-$19: per-type values, and two by $AD9A
regions.description: $8C98 is the handler of types $18 and $19 only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D), and it indexes with LDY $0500,X, the type: LDA $8D50,Y ($8C9D) reads $8D68-$8D69 and $8D54,Y ($8CA3) reads $8D6C-$8D6D. $8D34: JSR $AD9A / TAY / LDA $8D6E,Y -> $15 reads from $8D6E; the code at $8D70 bounds it at two entries, but $AD9A's range is NOT established. $8D6A-$8D6B have no reader - they would be types $1A-$1B of the first table.

regions.name: Types $24-$26: three per-type values
regions.description: $8E68 is the handler of types $24, $25 and $26 (bank 6 dispatch). LDY $0500,X, then LDA $900D,Y -> $0560, $9010,Y -> $07A0, $9013,Y -> $07D0 ($8E6D-$8E78) - so the bytes read are $9031-$9033, $9034-$9036 and $9037-$9039. Nine bytes, ending exactly on the code at $903A.

regions.name: Types $10-$13: value for $0560
regions.description: $9C1D is the handler of types $10-$13 only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D). LDY $0500,X / LDA $9CDE,Y: the type indexes from $9CDE, so the bytes read are $9CEE-$9CF1.

regions.name: Offset wave, 16 entries
regions.description: ADC $9CF2,Y at $9CBE, added to $0518 (the object's position) into $07A0. Values 00 04 08 0C 10 0C 08 04 00 FC F8 F4 F0 F4 F8 FC - one period of a triangle wave. Y there comes from $FE88 or is forced to 0; its range is NOT established, so the 16 is structural (it ends where the type-indexed reads of $9CF2 begin, at $9CF2 + $10).

regions.name: Types $10-$13: value for $07D0
regions.description: LDA $9CF2,Y with Y = the type ($10-$13) at $9C28, so the bytes read are $9D02-$9D05, stored in $07D0 and later ANDed with $07B8 as a mask.

regions.name: Types $10-$13: value by animation frame
regions.description: LDA #$40 / LDY #$04 / JSR $C0A5 ($CD7A, an animation counter returning Y below the limit passed in Y, so 0-3), then LDA $9D06,Y (at $9CDA) / JSR $A1E7. Four bytes, ending exactly on the code at $9D0A.

regions.name: Two 7-byte tables indexed by $4B
regions.description: $9EC3: LDY $4B, LDA $9EDE,Y -> $07B8 and $07A0, LDA $9EE5,Y -> $07D0. Bases seven apart, and $4B starts at 1 (bank 0 $8101, or 2 at $8126), so Y is 1-7 and each read starts one byte early - $9EDE is the last byte of the code before. $4B is the shield bar length on the status screen.

regions.name: Table indexed by $4A
regions.description: $9EF6: LDY $4A / LDA $9EEC,Y -> $0698. $4A is the attack level, 1-4 ($FD0E caps it at 4; it starts at 1), so the bytes read are $9EED-$9EF0 - four entries, ending exactly on the code at $9EF1. It was a lead until $FD0E fixed the range.

regions.name: Types $14-$15: value for $0548
regions.description: $A26E is the handler of types $14 and $15 only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D), and it indexes with LDY $0500,X, the type: LDA $A2B0,Y ($A273), so the bytes read are $A2C4-$A2C5, ending on the table $A2C6 that the same handler reads by animation frame.

regions.name: Types $55-$57: two per-type values
regions.description: $A349 is the handler of types $55, $56 and $57 only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D), and it indexes with LDY $0500,X, the type: LDA $A385,Y ($A354) -> $07B8 and $A388,Y ($A35A). Bases three apart: two 3-byte tables, ending exactly on the animation table at $A3E0. CORRECTION: the $A3E0 region said these six bytes had no reader.

regions.name: Table by 10-frame animation counter
regions.description: $A38B: LDY #$0A / JSR $C0A5 (Y = counter 0-9) / LDA $A3E0,Y, compared with $67, and again at $A3C4 with Y = $0638,X, the same counter. Ten entries, ending exactly on the code at $A3EA. The six bytes before it are the type tables at $A3DA.

regions.name: Ends of two tables read by $A497
regions.description: $A4A5: LDA $A4EE,Y for Y below $0C, and $A4AE: LDA $A4DD,Y for Y $1C-$1D. With the code before them ending at $A4F7, only Y = $0A-$0B of the first ($A4F8-$A4F9) and Y = $1C-$1D of the second ($A4F9-$A4FA) read data; the two share $A4F9. The range of Y is NOT established.

regions.name: Types $5A-$5C: four per-type values
regions.description: $A507 is the handler of types $5A, $5B and $5C only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D), and it indexes with LDY $0500,X, the type: LDA $A546,Y ($A50C) -> $0560, $A549,Y -> $0698, $A54C,Y -> $07A0 and $A54F,Y. Each base plus $5A-$5C lands here: four 3-byte tables, 12 bytes, ending exactly on the flip table at $A5AC.

regions.name: Sprite flip bits by animation frame
regions.description: LDY #$04 / JSR $C0A5 (Y = 0-3), then $0560 AND #$03 ORA $A5AC,Y, at $A56F and $A6FA. Values 00 80 C0 40: none, vertical, both, horizontal. Four entries, ending exactly on the code at $A5B0. The twelve bytes before it are the type tables at $A5A0.

regions.name: Types $50-$51: four per-type values
regions.description: $A703 is the handler of types $50 and $51 only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D), and it indexes with LDY $0500,X, the type: LDA $A716,Y ($A708) -> $0698, $A718,Y -> $0560, $A71A,Y -> $07B8, $A71C,Y. Bases two apart, types $50-$51: four 2-byte tables, 8 bytes, ending on the code at $A76E. $A80E reads $A713, $A715 and $A719 with a Y that lands inside the same bytes; its Y is NOT established.

regions.name: Types $36-$37: value for $0560
regions.description: $A8D8 is the handler of types $36 and $37 only (bank 6 dispatch $80DE/$815D), and it indexes with LDY $0500,X, the type: LDA $A982,Y ($A8E0), so the bytes read are $A9B8-$A9B9. The five bytes after, $A9BA-$A9BE (FE 02 FF 01 00), have no reader found.

regions.name: Tile rectangles: 5 x 4x4, by $0638
regions.description: $A991: $16/$17 = $A9BF + 16 x A, then $15 = $14 = 4 and JMP $C07E, the rectangle blit - so each entry is a 4 x 4 block of background tiles, drawn at the object's position. A is the object's $0638 (or 3, from $A98B). Five entries fill $A9BF-$AA0E exactly, ending on the code at $AA0F; the count is structural.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 4 x 4
regions.description: $AC7A: $16/$17 = $AC8F, width $15 = height $14 = 4, JMP $C07E (the rectangle blit $D99C). 16 bytes, ending exactly on the code at $AC9F.

regions.name: Values by $07B8, read with Y from 1
regions.description: $AD0C: STA $07B8,X / TAY / LDA $AD89,Y -> $0560, then $AD8D,Y -> $05D8. Y comes out of a fold of the value above into 0-4; Y = 0 would read the code byte at $AD89 and Y = 4 the next table's first byte, so the table as bounded here holds Y = 1-3. Whether 0 and 4 occur is NOT established.

regions.name: Tile rectangles 2 x 4, five entries
regions.description: $B43F: $16/$17 from A/Y, width $15 = 2, height $14 = 4, JMP $C07E. The callers pass $B454 ($B43B), $B458 and $B460 ($B415/$B40F), $B468 ($B5B5) and $B470 ($B5BF) - so the first two overlap by four bytes on purpose, and the last ends exactly on the code at $B478.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 6 x 6
regions.description: $B5FB: width $15 = height $14 = 6, $16/$17 = $B60F, JMP $C07E. 36 bytes, ending exactly on the code at $B633.

regions.name: Tile rectangles 4 x 2, four entries
regions.description: $B787: $16/$17 = $B79D + 8 x A, width $15 = 4, height $14 = 2, JMP $B449 (the blit). A is 3 at $B785, or at $B73D the frame counter from $C0A5 with limit 4 and 3 folded to 1 - so entries 0-3. 4 x 8 = 32 bytes, ending exactly on the code at $B7BD.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 2 x 2
regions.description: $BAB8-$BAC7: width $15 = height $14 = 2, $16/$17 = $BBBB, JSR $C07E.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 6 x 4 (or its first 3 rows)
regions.description: $BB80-$BB8F: height $14 = 3 or 4, width $15 = 6, $16/$17 = $BBBF, JSR $C07E. 6 x 4 = 24 bytes, ending exactly where the next rectangle begins.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 6 x 2
regions.description: $BAEA: JSR $BB80 (which leaves $15 = 6; $D99C counts in $11 and does not touch $15), then height $14 = 2, $16/$17 = $BBD7, JMP $C07E. 12 bytes, ending exactly where $BBE3's reads begin.

regions.name: Table indexed by $B9, the scroll speed high byte
regions.description: LDY $B9 / LDA $BBE3,Y -> $07D0 at $BA95 (an object using metasprite $1A). $B8/$B9 is the corridor scroll speed (bank 7 $E68F-$E69B step it by 2). Values 64 96 C8 FA FA FA FA FA FA = 100, 150, 200, then 250. The extent runs to the code at $BBEC; the range of $B9 is NOT established.

regions.name: Three direction offsets
regions.description: $BE54: LDY $14 / LDA $BEAE,Y with Y counting 2, 1, 0 - added to $15 and stored in $0788 of each of three objects spawned there (type $17). Values 02 FE 00.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 6 x 5
regions.description: $BDF8-$BE07: $16/$17 = $BEB1, width $15 = 6, height $14 = 3 or 5, blitted by $C07E through $BEA3. 6 x 5 = 30 bytes, ending exactly where the next rectangle begins.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 6 x 1
regions.description: $BE15-$BE1F: $16/$17 = $BECF, height $14 = 1 with width still 6, then JSR $C07E. Six bytes.

regions.name: Tile rectangle 6 x 6
regions.description: $BE92-$BEA1: $15 = $14 = 6, $16/$17 = $BED5, then $BEA3 blits it. 36 bytes, ending on the code at $BEF9. With the three tables before it this partitions $BEAE-$BEF8 exactly, 75 of 75 bytes.

regions.name: 2x2 tile groups for $C054
regions.description: $D865 (entry $C054) draws a 2x2 block with its attribute. When A AND 3 is non-zero it reads the four tiles from $D8E0 + A ... $D8E3 + A (LDA $D8E0,Y with Y = A); when it is zero it uses A, A+1 ... directly. So A itself is the byte offset into this table and any A with a low bit set names a group; the groups can overlap. The extent is structural - the last byte of $D865's code is at $D8E0 and $D92D is code - and which groups are actually used depends on callers not enumerated here.

regions.name: TGL game: corridor order
regions.description: $ECFC: LDY $77 / INC $77 / LDA $ED08,Y / STA $51 / JMP $EC94 - the next corridor, reached only when $30 bit 1 is set (the TGL password's corridors-only game) after the reward screen. $77 starts at 0 ($EB18). 1, 11, 12, 2, 13, 3, 14, 4, 15, 5, 16, 6, 17, 7, 18, 8, 19, 9, 20, 10, 21: every corridor 1-21 exactly once, which is the check on the 21 entries; after 21 $ECBD takes the ending path instead of reading a 22nd.

regions.name: Labyrinth music, by area
regions.description: LDA $EF16,Y with Y = $50, the labyrinth area (bank 7 $EBB0, $EF10 and $FFDE), then JSR/JMP $D852 - the play-sound call - so one song per labyrinth area 0-10. 11 entries, ending where the next table's reads begin at $EF21. Values 09 07 07 02 02 07 0D 07 02 0D 0E.

regions.name: Corridor sound, first 9 corridors
regions.description: LDA $EF21,Y with Y = $51, the corridor, at $EEAF; zero means nothing, otherwise JMP $D852. Only 9 bytes lie between $EF21 and the next table at $EF2A, so corridors 9 and up read that table's bytes - either they never reach this code or the overlap is deliberate. THE 9 IS STRUCTURAL; a LEAD.

regions.name: Corridor music, by corridor
regions.description: LDA $EF2A,Y with Y = $51 then JSR $D852 at $ECB3. 22 entries, corridors 0-21, ending where $EF40 begins. The values repeat in pairs and then repeat 1-10 for 11-20 - corridors 1-2 share a song, 3-4 another, and corridor n+10 plays what corridor n does - the same pairing the scenes ($EF55) and keys follow.

regions.name: Corridor reward item, by corridor
regions.description: $EE1D: JSR $EECC, and when the result has bit 7 set, AND #$7F / TAY / LDA $EF40,Y / STA $55. 21 entries, ending where $EF55 begins. $EE1D reaches this for a corridor-entrance record; once that corridor is cleared the entrance is screen 5, whose controller $9F75 sets out a type-$31 item in slot 5 - so $55 is the corridor's reward item, an icon number (corridor 0's 25 is never used: there is no entrance 0). CORRECTION to 'what $55 selects is NOT established'. Whether the reward can be taken more than once is not established.

regions.name: Corridor scene, by corridor
regions.description: $EF74: LDY $51 / $EF76 LDA $EF55,Y / STA $5C / JSR bank 5 $8000 - the scene (tiles, metatile sets, palettes, see tools/tgl/scene.py) each corridor loads after scene 1. 22 entries, corridors 0-21, ending exactly where the code at $EF6C begins. Values 32 for corridor 0, then pairs 33-38; 11-20 repeat 1-10. HARDWARE: a savestate in corridor 15 has $5C = $23 = $EF55[15].

regions.name: Key awarded by corridors 1-10
regions.description: $F4A7: LDY $51 (the corridor) / BEQ / CPY #$0B / BCC - so corridors 1-10 only - LDA $F6DA,Y. $F4B7 passes the same value to the far call to bank 2 $8006, the key-icon builder, after LDA #$81 / STA $0500 / ORA $04B0 / STA $04B0 on the key inventory. Values 1 2 3 4 0 5 0 6 7 0. Checked against the world map: corridor n gives the key that labyrinth area n+1 needs (areas 1-10 need 0,1,2,3,4,4,5,5,6,7), and corridors 5, 7 and 10 give none because the next area needs a key already held.

regions.name: Aiming thresholds: tan(33.75, 22.5, 11.25 degrees) x 256
regions.description: $F8BE: CMP $F95A,Y for Y = 3 down to 1 against the ratio min(|dx|,|dy|) x 256 / max(|dx|,|dy|) that $F9B6 divides out. AB 6A 32 = 171, 106, 50; tan 33.75 = 0.668 (171), tan 22.5 = 0.414 (106), tan 11.25 = 0.199 (51). So the step Y (0-3) is which of four 22.5-degree slices of an octant the direction falls in. Y is never 0 at the compare, so the read base is one byte early; $F95A is the RTS before.

regions.name: Aiming: octant and step to one of 16 directions
regions.description: $F8C6: TYA / ORA $38 / TAY / LDA $F95E,Y. $F863 builds $38 from the two objects' positions: bit 2 = the target is left, bit 3 = above, bit 4 = the vertical distance is the larger. With the step 0-3 from the thresholds, Y covers 0-31 and every value in the table is 0-15 - a direction in sixteenths of a turn. 32 bytes, ending exactly where the tables at $F97E begin.

regions.name: Player attack by attack level, and a value by mode
regions.description: $FD0E: LDY $4A / CPY #$04 / BCC / LDY #$04 - capped at 4, and $4A starts at 1 - then LDA $FD4A,Y ($FD18) -> $05A8, slot 0's attack: 1 2 3 5. Then $FD44: LDA $FD4F,Y -> $0698 with Y = 0 or 2 (from $0590 below or above 5) plus 1 when $30 bit 6 is set: 03 05 41 06. 4 + 4 bytes, ending on the code at $FD53. This also confirms that $4A is 1-4.

regions.name: DMC sample: 17 zero bytes (a timer, not a sound)
regions.description: Bank 6 $802A writes $4012 = $FF (sample address $C000 + $FF x 64 = $FFC0) and $4013 = $01 (length 1 x 16 + 1 = 17 bytes), with $4011 = $00. These are those 17 bytes, all zero, so the channel outputs silence; the point is the sample-finished IRQ, which the handler at $DCF3 uses to time the raster split. $FFC0 is 64-byte aligned, as the DMC requires.
